He then appointed himself chief of the armed forces, with the rank of colonel, and effectively controlled the five-member Presidency.  He maintained this control through a string of puppet presidents until 1940, when he was himself elected President of Cuba on a populist platform.  He then instated the 1940 Constitution of Cuba, considered progressive for its time, and served until 1944.
